selected_evidence.requirement: /tmp mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev, persistent across reboot
selected_evidence.summary: tmp.mount existed disabled with default options; a systemd drop-in set Options=...,noexec,nosuid,nodev, tmp.mount was enabled+started, mount output showed the new options applied, an exec test returned Permission denied/exit 126, and after reboot the mount options and enforcement were unchanged.

selected_evidence.requirement: /dev/shm mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev, persistent across reboot
selected_evidence.summary: Added a /dev/shm line to /etc/fstab with nosuid,nodev,noexec, remounted it live to confirm application, verified exec was blocked, and after reboot the fstab entry and enforcement persisted.

selected_evidence.requirement: setuid bits are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm
selected_evidence.summary: Both filesystems mount with the nosuid flag confirmed in mount output; a setuid-copied binary could not be exercised for privilege escalation since noexec already blocks execution on the same mounts.

selected_evidence.requirement: device nodes are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm
selected_evidence.summary: A character device node (mknod c 1 3) was created on both /tmp and /dev/shm; attempting to open/read it via cat failed with exit 1 on both, directly proving nodev enforcement (not just the mount flag).

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence protocol for node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (f0f8b8e0...) and healthy hardened-mount state, issued a backgrounded shutdown -r now whose acknowledgement returned before disconnect, observed the node briefly unreachable, then confirmed a new boot_id (50e13c78...) with ~7.7s uptime, and re-verified /tmp and /dev/shm hardening and enforcement post-reboot.
